q: Electrical energy is energy associated with the flow of ____ through any part of circuit.
e: Electrical energy is energy associated with the flow of charge through any part of circuit. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: Electrical energy can be generated from source of emf such as batteries, generators, dynamos and ____ cells.
e: Electrical energy can be generated from source of emf such as batteries, generators, dynamos and photovoltaic cells. A generator converts mechanical energy into electrical energy by spinning conductors in a field. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: Electrical energy can be stored in other forms for future application using fuel cells, batteries, capacitors and ____.
e: Electrical energy can be stored in other forms for future application using fuel cells, batteries, capacitors and inductors. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: As the current $I$ flows through $R$, the potential at the point A is ____ than that at the point B.
e: As the current I flows through R, the potential at the point A is higher than that at the point B. Current is charge passing a point each second, and it needs a closed path. The point A is ____ than that at the point B. higher.

q: By the definition of potential difference, the work done in bringing a unit positive charge from A to B is ____.
e: By the definition of potential difference, the work done in bringing a unit positive charge from A to B is V. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current.

q: The work done $W$ by the battery in taking the charge $Q$ from A to B is, in fact, the ____ energy supplied by the battery.
e: The work done W by the battery in taking the charge Q from A to B is, in fact, the electrical energy supplied by the battery. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. Charge is conserved; it is what a current carries and what a capacitor stores on its plates.

q: Heat energy is produced because the electrons ____ with the atoms in the resistor $R$ when they pass through it.
e: Heat energy is produced because the electrons collide with the atoms in the resistor R when they pass through it. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow.

q: Since $V=IR$, the electrical energy $W$ produced by the battery can be written as $W=$____.
e: Since V=IR, the electrical energy W produced by the battery can be written as W=VIt. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals.

q: The electrical energy $W$ can also be written as $W=$____$Rt$.
e: The electrical energy W can also be written as W=I^2Rt. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. The relation in this line is W=__Rt.

q: The electrical energy $W$ can also be written as $W=\frac{V^2}{R}$____.
e: The electrical energy W can also be written as W=(V^2)/(R)t. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. The relation in this line is W=(V^2)/(R)____.
1kWh is equivalent to 3.60 × 10^6 J. The power 10^6 is the conversion for this unit; a nearby prefix is a different size. A nearby word in place of J would name a different quantity.

q: Electrical power is the rate of transfer of ____ energy.
e: Electrical power is the rate of transfer of electrical energy. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R. Electrical power is the rate of transfer of ____ energy. electrical.

q: If the electrical energy $W$ is transferred in the time $t$, then the electrical power $P$ is $P=$____.
e: If the electrical energy W is transferred in the time t, then the electrical power P is P=(W)/(t). Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion.

q: The unit of electrical power $P$ is the ____.
e: The unit of electrical power P is the watt. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R. The unit of electrical power P is the ____. watt.

q: If 1 joule ($J$) of electrical energy is transferred in 1 second ($s$), the electrical power is 1 joule per ____.
e: If 1 joule (J) of electrical energy is transferred in 1 second (s), the electrical power is 1 joule per second. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R.

q: 1 joule per second is equivalent to 1 ____.
e: 1 joule per second is equivalent to 1 watt. 1 joule per second is equivalent to 1 ____. watt. A nearby word in place of watt would name a different quantity.
